children: Rising interest rates in the U.S. have likely capped the performance of Singapore's small- and mid-cap stocks, say Macquarie Capital analysts in a note, citing historical trading patterns. Higher rates have likely prevented these small-to-mid-cap stocks from reaping the full benefits of the latest tranche of funds under Singapore's equities development market program meant to boost trading in small- and mid-cap stocks, the analysts say. Overall liquidity has been declining and stock liquidity has pivoted back towards larger caps, they say. Macquarie analysts remain focused on companies with strong, visible earnings growth, such as UOB-Kay Hian and UMS Integration. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
